output.evidence: Version 2 delivers the cleaner finished set within the Zellige Noon Water Court concept: the glazed basil-green wall meets the continuous tiled ground on a single credible baseline, the flacon stands right-of-centre with a soft contact shadow seated into the grout, and the left editorial column (wide-tracked Guerlain line, four-line Baskerville-style serif title, honey-gold rule) holds a stable vertical overlap with the cap/shoulder zone and clean horizontal separation. Version 1 is undermined by a hard diagonal shadow raking across the left wall and floor, which contradicts the declared noon top-light horizontal band at the wall base, dirties the quiet冷绿 text column and reads as an off-frame artifact rather than campaign lighting; its bottle contact is also flatter. Version 2's tile glaze, grout rhythm and gold-stop highlights are more controlled and its typography spacing is more even.
remaining_problems: Version 2 shows a faint ghosted bottle-shaped outline etched into the upper-centre tile field, a generation artifact on the wall
The scalloped fish-scale tile row near the wall base departs from the declared uniform vertical zellige column pattern
The promised sharp horizontal noon shadow band at the wall base is only weakly implied; the wall-floor junction reads slightly bright and flat
Contact shadow under the flacon is soft and shallow rather than clearly sunk into a grout joint
